rule.description: A function or method in this repository reads and writes several data members of one site record instance it does not own, while touching its own instance's data less often, instead of asking the record for the behavior that is built on that data. Direct attribute loads and stores on the record count as data access, and so does delegation through trivial per-field getters or setters (get_<field>/set_<field> of a field the record class stores); asking the record to act through a real behavior method does not.

checks.description: Detect methods that reach directly and repeatedly into several data members of one site record instance instead of delegating to the record. Direct attribute loads and stores as well as trivial per-field get_<field>/set_<field> delegation of stored record fields all count as data reach; real behavior methods of the record do not.
checks.detected_relation: consumer -> data members of the site record (app.api.model.Site)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The consumer is more interested in the data of the site record than in the data of its own instance: the file-name convention, the on-disk location, the enabled/disabled encoding, the loaded content, and the modification time of the record are all manipulated from outside the record class, so the record is a bare data holder whose behavior is scattered across its collaborators.

matches.evidence: SiteRegistry.find matches by record.filename.startswith(name), opens io.open(os.path.join(record.config_path, record.filename)), and stuffs the file contents into record.content itself, instead of asking the record to recognize the name and load its content.

SiteEditor.apply_update matches records through record.filename.startswith(name) and rewrites the file behind record.config_path/record.filename with io.open(..., 'w'), instead of asking the matched record to store the new content.

SiteEditor.remove matches records through record.filename.startswith(name), deletes the file at os.path.join(record.config_path, record.filename) with os.remove, and re-checks os.path.exists on the record's location, instead of asking the record to delete itself.

SiteEditor.set_state splits the disabled marker off record.filename, renames the file under record.config_path to the reassembled name, and relies on the record's raw file name for both activation and deactivation, instead of asking the record to activate or deactivate itself.

DomainOverview.cards derives the displayed name and the enabled state from record.filename, picks the card timestamp from record.modified, and appends the suffix-stripped name for disabled records, instead of asking the record for its card data.

excluded.reason: The endpoint reads only record.filename (state marker) and record.content (2 data accesses, single purpose: passing the loaded content to the template) after asking the registry to find the record; this is presentation of the returned value, not repeated manipulation of several data members, and stays below the rule's reach threshold.
The creation path composes one path through its own registry collaborator and never touches a site record, so no record data is read or written here.
The configuration-file endpoints operate on the nginx configuration directory only; no site record exists in this scope.

The site record itself only carries data at this stage; it performs no work on another type's data, so it cannot be an envious consumer.
